source.title: On the Validity of Modeling SGD with Stochastic Differential Equations (SDEs)
source.authors: Zhiyuan Li; Sadhika Malladi; Sanjeev Arora

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present. Some reported accuracy and error values appear only in figures.
record.tranche_reason: The study reports training-accuracy or training-error outcomes for SGD-based training on vision datasets, which bear on V1. Its focus is comparing SGD with SDE-related processes and examining linear scaling, rather than directly testing the catalog’s full claim.
record.gate_note: Training curves and batch-size error plots bear on V1. The study does not state that these runs use random initialization or give exact training-error values for the plotted curves. Other claim versions are discussed only indirectly or are not tested.
record.test_reason: The study reports its own SGD training classification accuracy/error on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100, using the method and measure named in V1. However, the supplied text preserves figure axes and captions without readable curve values, so near-zero training error cannot be established.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: SVAG provably approaches the canonical order-1 Itô SDE under stated assumptions and empirically approximates it efficiently; the SDE tracks SGD in many tested settings. The authors derive and experimentally assess a necessary condition for SDE fidelity and linear scaling, with failures in some settings. They do not conclude that these networks universally reach zero training error.
record.recipe_differences: The study compares SGD, Gaussian-noise gradient descent, and SVAG as tests of an SDE approximation; it does not use the claim versions’ recipes for isolating training error or initialization.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported SDE/SGD agreement varies with batch size and normalization; the authors report failures for large-batch settings and for GroupNorm architectures on CIFAR-100.

fits_no_version.finding: SGD and covariance-matched NGD have similar training and test curves.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Replacing SGD noise with Gaussian noise of matching covariance can preserve training and generalization behavior in the tested CIFAR-10 settings.

fits_no_version.finding: The SDE approximation and linear scaling rule can fail at large learning rates/batch sizes; GroupNorm CIFAR-100 experiments also show an SDE mismatch.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SDE fidelity and linear scaling have conditions involving discretization and the gradient noise-to-signal ratio. These results do not measure V5's stability-threshold and curvature behavior.

record.problems: Training-accuracy and training-error outcomes relevant to V1 are presented in plots without exact textual values. Random initialization is not stated. Common random-shuffling experiments fall outside the stated SVAG theory.

untested.parts: Corrupted/random labels, Adam, and controlled comparisons of smaller models, early stopping, and regularization. Random initialization is not documented in the supplied experimental description. CIFAR-100 training error is measured, but its values cannot be recovered here.
Teacher-student ReLU problems, spurious-minimum frequencies, and extra-neuron interventions.
Matched depth comparisons with and without identity shortcuts, special tanh initialization, and Fixup.
Initialization interventions, signal/gradient propagation, and trainable-depth comparisons.
Learning rates relative to initial linearized stability thresholds, curvature trajectories, catapult recovery, and full-batch edge-of-stability behavior.
No readable result establishes a BatchNorm speed or learning-rate-tolerance advantage over an otherwise matched network without normalization; Fixup is not tested.

record.verdict_notes: No support, scope-limit, or challenge verdict is justified from unreadable curve values. Similarity between two training curves and reported test accuracies cannot establish near-zero training classification error. BatchNorm-versus-GroupNorm performance comparisons do not isolate V6's normalization-versus-no-normalization effect.

versions.untested_parts: Random initialization, CIFAR-100 training classification error, corrupted or random labels, and the stated smaller-model, early-stopping, and regularization comparisons are not tested here. Training-accuracy and training-error outcomes are plotted, but exact values are not stated in the text.
